Carlos — thanks, and appreciated the template. Quick answers up front so procurement can proceed: 

1) Egress addressing options we support (choose one in the SOW):
   - Dedicated static egress IPs (per-customer NAT block): guaranteed static outbound IPs with SLA-backed assignment.
   - Shared Redwood egress pool (ephemeral NAT): lower operational friction but IPs are shared across customers; we provide CIDR and SNI allowlist guidance.

2) TLS/SNI and certing:
   - All control-plane and model-serving connections use TLS 1.2+ (RSA/ECDSA).
   - We present service-level CNs (api.redwood-inference.net) for hosted callbacks; for private deployments we support mutually agreed CNs or mTLS per request.

3) Ports/FQDNs: we'll provide a minimal FQDN list for telemetry, package updates, and license checks — and a supplemental allowlist for external model-hinting endpoints.

4) IP rotation notice: our standard is 14 days notice; for Brightwell we can offer 30 days notice with an emergency rotation process documented in the runbook. That change will be expressed as an amendment to the SOW.

5) Forced-proxy support: supported. If Brightwell provides an outbound HTTP/TLS proxy (or a NAT gateway), Redwood will route egress through it and provide the signed TLS root/cert fingerprints required for inspection. Differences (proxy vs Redwood NAT) are listed in the proposed clause below.

I'm looping in Marissa (sales, contractual), Laura (PM for Private), Ben (security/compliance) and Olga (infrastructure) to produce the connection stencil + evidence pack. Expect a draft within 48 hours. If Brightwell needs the clause faster for the redline, tell me which one of the two addressing options they prefer.
